title: Runtime fidelity surgeon manual
author: Alexandra M. Rivera
content:
Summary
-------
This manual describes the end-to-end process and operational discipline we use to change inference fidelity inside the runtime: any deliberate change that affects numeric precision, kernel selection, batching policy, KV-cache warmup, model variant selection, or routing heuristics that we expect to change latency/cost/quality tradeoffs. The document combines architecture rationale, kernel scheduling implications, profiling playbook steps, benchmarking commands, an acceptance gate checklist, and example release-note scaffolding.

Scope
-----
- Applies to hosted, dedicated, and private deployments for production traffic.
- Covers automated changes (autotune controller), manual operator interventions, and canary rollouts.
- Excludes model training changes, prompt-level A/B experiments, and customer-visible prompt edits.

When to perform fidelity surgery
-----------------------------
Perform a fidelity change only when one or more of the following are true: 
1) measurable unit-cost savings (>5% projected) with acceptable quality risk;
2) latency SLO headroom is low and a fidelity change is required to meet tail SLOs;
3) a hardware constraint (GPU memory, thermal ceiling) necessitates an alternate execution path;
4) quality regressions are explicitly tolerated for degraded tiers (e.g., fallback fast path).

Before you start (preflight checklist)
------------------------------------
- Ownership: confirm an owner from runtime-ops and an owner from applied-ml (names and PagerDuty rotation).
- Ticketing: create a ticket with hypothesis, target metric delta, and rollback conditions.
- Canary targets: identify traffic cohorts and snapshot corresponding request surfaces.
- Baseline captures: collect 1 hour of traces for the target cohort including kernel traces, KV-cache hit rates, per-token cost, and example outputs (min 100 sessions).
- Evaluation prompts: select at least 200 prompt/test pairs from the eval harness tagged for quality regressions.

Architecture considerations that inform changes
----------------------------------------------
- Kernel selection is orthogonal to model architecture; the runtime maps model ops to kernel families at dispatch time. Changes in kernel hints may increase occupancy and change preemption behavior.
- Prefetch and KV-cache warmup interact with quantized execution: warmup patterns that assume FP16 cache layouts may be less effective for int8 kernels.
- Priority-driven scheduler treats fidelity-change traffic as "deferred candidate" until canary passes; this prevents accidental priority inversion.

Operator runbook: step-by-step
-----------------------------
1) Prepare canary image/config: increment feature flag and attach a unique trace tag (fidelity-surgeon-<ticket-id>).
2) Dry-run locally: use the shadow harness to replay captured traces against the new kernel/code path with shadow traffic enabled (no live responses).
   - Command: 
     ./bin/shadow-replay --trace-file=baseline-traces.tar.gz --kernel-hint=int8-micro --concurrency=20 --output=shadow-report.json
3) Run microbenchmarks on the intended hardware slice (3 runs):
   - Per-token latency (p50/p95/p99)
   - Kernel invocation time distribution (collect CUDA/NVTX traces)
   - Memory high-water mark and fragmentation sample
4) Canary rollout: begin with 0.5% traffic to a stable pool with increased logging and a non-blocking guard. Monitor for 30 minutes.
5) Expand canary: if health signals remain green, expand to 5% for 2 hours, then to 25% for 12 hours.
6) Full rollout: gradually promote to 100% using the rollout matrix in the Acceptance section.

Key monitoring signals (must be green during canary)
---------------------------------------------------
- SLOs: request p99 latency relative delta <= 10% and absolute p99 inside SLA target.
- Errors: request error rate increase <= 0.01% absolute; business-critical routes require 0 increase.
- Quality: BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-sim metrics on eval prompts must be within the regression gate (default: < 1.5% quality loss).
- Cost: per-token CPU/GPU time reduction >= projected threshold.
- Kernel health: no new kernel OOMs, kernel launch errors, or NVML thermal spikes.

Profiling playbook excerpts
--------------------------
- Sampling plan: stratified sampling across short/medium/long sequences, chat vs. single-call, and top-ten customer tenants.
- Tools and commands:
  - nvprof/Nsight: capture GPU kernel timelines for the benchmark trial. Example: 
    nsight-sys profile --output=nsys-report.nsys --trace=cuda,nvtx --duration=120 ./serve-bench --profile-target=canary-pool
  - Kernel traces: ensure kernel names are mapped to canonical IDs using the kernel-mapper utility: 
    python tools/kernel-mapper.py --input nsys-report.nsys --output kernel-latency.csv
  - Per-request trace: use the trace-correlator to stitch system-level traces to request IDs: 
    ./trace-correlator --trace-dir traces/ --tag fidelity-surgeon-1234 --out stitched.json

Benchmarking suite: what to run and why
--------------------------------------
- Microbenchmarks: single-batch synthetic runs to measure kernel latency and occupancy at fixed sequence lengths.
- Replay benchmarks: replay captured production traffic with preserved inter-arrival timing. This shows end-to-end behavior (queueing, batching).
- Shadow A/B: run new path in shadow mode with sampling of produced outputs for offline quality scoring.
- Cost simulation: feed kernel-level latencies into the cost model to project monthly delta.

Example bench commands
----------------------
- Synthetic micro: 
  ./bench/micro --model rwind-7b --batch-size 1 --seq-len 256 --kernel-profile > micro-256.log
- Replay: 
  ./bench/replay --trace traces/capture-20261001.tar.gz --scale 1.0 --inject-tag fidelity-surgeon-5678 --out replay-report.json

Kernel scheduling knobs and notes
--------------------------------
- Admission window: reduce admission window for int8 kernels to avoid long head-of-line blocking with high-occupancy kernels. Typical knob: runtime.scheduler.admission_ms (default 3ms) -> 1.5ms for micro-kernel heavy workloads.
- Priority decay: lower priority decay to bias warmup cohorts into prefetch success for cache-sensitive flows.
- Cooperative preemption: enable for high-mix pools when deploying new kernels to help prevent starvation. Flag: runtime.scheduler.coop_preempt=true.
- Kernel crediting: track kernel cost units per-request and enforce soft quotas to limit noisy-neighbor impact.

Acceptance criteria (canary gates)
---------------------------------
Table: acceptance thresholds (must be strings per JSON schema but presented in a table-like block)

- SLO_p99: "<= baseline_p99 * 1.10"
- Error_rate_delta: "<= 0.0001 (absolute)"
- Eval_quality_pass: ">= 98.5% of baseline score on eval set (configurable)"
- Cost_delta: ">= projected_savings OR documented justification for cost-neutral change"
- Kernel_stability: "0 kernel OOMs, 0 new kernel launch errors in canary window"

Rollback plan
-------------
- Immediate rollback triggers: any of the following should trigger an automated rollback and pager:
  1) p99 latency > acceptance threshold for 3 consecutive measurement windows (5-minute windows).
  2) quality regression detected above tolerance on sampled outputs.
  3) kernel crash, OOM, or interconnect fault.
- Rollback procedure:
  1) Flip feature flag to previous image using the rollout controller: 
     ./rolloutctl promote --target previous --tag fidelity-surgeon-1234 --reason "auto-rollback"
  2) Confirm system converges and monitor the same signals for 30 minutes.
  3) Create incident ticket and attach all artifacts (nsys report, stitched traces, shadow-report.json).

Known issues and mitigation notes
--------------------------------
- Int8 microkernels show sporadic latency spikes at p99 on sequence length > 1024 due to tensor-slice alignment. Mitigation: apply kernel alignment patch (K-alignment-v2) or restrict int8 to seq<=1024.
- KV-cache warmup mismatch: quantized kernels may interpret KV padding differently; run the kv-warmup-mapper job during canary.
- Scheduler hysteresis: rapid fidelity flips can cause scheduler thrashing; enforce a 30-minute minimum cool-down on pool-level knob changes.
- Observability gaps: early int8 rollouts may not tag kernel names correctly in legacy telemetry; ensure kernel-mapper version >= 2.12.

Release note template (for product/release notes)
------------------------------------------------
Summary: "Runtime: deploy int8 microkernel path for rwind-7b on production pools. Expected improvements: ~7% unit GPU cost reduction at p50 latency parity. Rollout: staged canary with automated rollback."
Impact: "Lower per-token cost; potential small quality drift in edge cases (long sequences)."
Rollout: "0.5% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 48 hours if gates pass."
Monitoring: "SLOs: request p99, kernel health, eval-quality snapshot for top 20 customers."
Known limitations: "Do not enable for on-prem clusters with older cuDNN versions (see compatibility table)."

Compatibility table (text)
- cuDNN >= 9.0: supported
- CUDA >= 12.2: recommended
- kernel-mapper >= 2.12: required for accurate telemetry

Operational ownership and contacts
----------------------------------
- Primary owner: runtime-ops (team alias: runtime-ops@redwood.com)
- Applied ML owner: applied-ml-evals@redwood.com
- PagerDuty escalation: runtime-pager (P1)

Postmortem and retrospective triggers
-------------------------------------
If a rollout hits an automated rollback or an unexpected quality regression, initiate a 72-hour postmortem with the following deliverables:
- Timeline of events (minute-level)
- Traces and profiles (NSYS, kernel-latency.csv)
- Hypothesis and test plan for next patch
- Action items and owners

Appendix: useful commands and scripts
------------------------------------
- Shadow replay harness: ./bin/shadow-replay --help
- Kernel mapper: python tools/kernel-mapper.py --help
- Rollout controller: ./rolloutctl status --tag fidelity-surgeon-1234
- Cost delta estimator: python tools/cost-sim.py --input replay-report.json --output cost-estimate.csv
